findings.title: Stale-listing test calls forgetStoppedLocked directly, not the Open path that captures bootGen
findings.body: The comment says "Open must not drop ownership on it", but the test reads `svc.bootGen` itself (1817) and calls `forgetStoppedLocked` with that value. The fix in `Open` is where `listGen` is read: before `Provider.List`, at service.go:717-720. If a later edit moved that read after the List call, the window would reopen and this test would still pass. Drive it through `Open`. For example, give the fake provider a List hook that finishes a boot of A during the listing, then check that `owned`/`parked` for A survive. Alternatively, reword the test as a unit test of the helper.

contracts.action: Park an owned device in the same save as the lease removal (endLeaseLocked → parkLocked), including Open's replaced-lease path
contracts.equivalent_path: finishRelease previously parked the device after releaseControl and Shutdown, in a later save (service.go:268-269). It still parks there, now through parkLocked.
contracts.before_after: Before: lease removal was saved first and the parked record only after finishRelease. A daemon stopping in between left an owned, running device with no lease and no parked record. After: parked is written under s.mu in the same saveLocked as the lease deletion (service.go:196-220). Open's replaced path (service.go:807) does the same before its save at service.go:817.
contracts.visible_effect: A simulator or emulator AO booted is powered off by retireParked after a restart, even if the daemon stopped mid-release.
contracts.failure_mode: If saveLocked fails, it is only logged (leasestore.go:120-122) and the record is lost as before. Close with shutdown=true that succeeds still deletes owned and parked (service.go:264-267). A device that is not owned is never parked (service.go:227). releaseIfGone deletes owned before endLeaseLocked (service.go:975-976), so a deleted device is not parked.

contracts.action: retireParked keeps the parked/owned records saved until Shutdown succeeds, and lists per platform
contracts.equivalent_path: releaseIfGone already uses ports.DevicePlatformLister, with the same fallback to List (service.go:956-960). The new listPlatform helper duplicates that logic but also filters the fallback's results by platform. The real provider's ListPlatform fails when that platform's listing failed (backend/internal/adapters/device/local/provider.go:601-604).
contracts.before_after: Before: one List call, and parked/owned were deleted and saved before Shutdown, then restored on failure. After: one listing per platform. A platform whose list failed is skipped and stays parked. Records are removed only after Shutdown returns nil. `releasing` blocks Open, pick and idle checks during the shutdown (service.go:393-397, 435-443, 787-790).
contracts.visible_effect: A running device is no longer forgotten, and so never powered off, when its platform listing failed while another platform's succeeded.
contracts.failure_mode: A failed Shutdown leaves the records in place and is retried on the next pass (logged at Warn). A failed per-platform list is logged at Debug and retried. The `!running` branch (service.go:382-390) is reached only after a clean list of that platform.

contracts.action: Skip forgetStoppedLocked when a boot finished since Open's listing began (bootGen)
contracts.equivalent_path: Open's pre-existing sequence of List, then forgetStoppedLocked, then pickLocked. forgetStoppedLocked's only caller is Open (service.go:727).
contracts.before_after: Before: a listing taken before a boot finished could show a just-booted owned device as off, and Open dropped ownership and the parked record. After: bootGen is read before List and incremented in boot()'s defer (service.go:1087). A mismatch skips the drop for that Open.
contracts.visible_effect: A just-booted simulator stays AO's, so it is powered off when its session ends, and is not left running unowned.
contracts.failure_mode: A boot that starts before the listing and finishes after changes bootGen, so the drop is skipped. A boot finished before listGen was read means the listing already shows the device running. A boot still in flight at drop time is excluded by idleLocked via s.booting. The cost of skipping is that cleanup of a user-stopped device is deferred to a later Open.

summary:
I found nothing that breaks in `service.go`. I reviewed the whole file plus `leasestore.go`. The three changes hold up against the code I read:

- **Park at lease removal:** `endLeaseLocked` now parks the device in the same save as the lease deletion.
- **`retireParked`:** it lists per platform and keeps the saved records until the shutdown succeeds, with `releasing` held meanwhile.
- **`bootGen`:** it stops a stale "off" listing from dropping ownership of a device that just booted.

I found one test gap: `TestAListingFromBeforeABootDropsNothing` calls `forgetStoppedLocked` directly, so it would not catch a regression in where `Open` reads `bootGen`. I could not run the tests.
